extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO and respondents in USPTO reciprocal-discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 implementing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) based on a state-court disbarment and setting procedural obligations (notice, response period, publication, compliance, and reinstatement steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal-discipline procedure under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' informs the respondent that the OED Director filed a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state court (exclusion from practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the Office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order must inform respondent that, to contest imposition of identical discipline, respondent shall file within 40 days a response 'containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact' that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Mailing by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent's official address and any address where the OED Director believes respondent receives mail is required; USPS delivery records may be relied upon. If respondent does not file a response, 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1) supports a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact and that identical discipline is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for imposing reciprocal exclusion (ethical disbarment/serious crime)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline here was based upon a state-court disbarment for ethical grounds and the respondent's admission to sufficient facts to crimes (credit card fraud, identity fraud, and larceny), each constituting a 'serious crime' as defined by S.J.C. Rule 4:01, § 12(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state disbarment based on ethical violations and/or convictions for serious crimes can justify reciprocal exclusion under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and § 11.59. Prior suspensions for failure to cooperate with bar counsel are relevant background considered in the reciprocal-discipline determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO (scope and effective date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is ordered 'excluded from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the Office, beginning on the date of this Final Order' for the violations specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies the scope (trademark and other non-patent law) and the effective date (the date of the Final Order). The exclusion is the identical discipline imposed by the state court as applied by the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent 'shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the text of § 11.58 is not reproduced in the order, the Final Order requires full compliance with its provisions (which govern duties of excluded practitioners, including client notification and handling of files). The order grants limited recognition to facilitate compliance with subsection (b) of § 11.58 (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice for 30 days to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is 'granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date this Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after the date this Final Order is signed for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is narrowly time-limited (30 days) and solely to allow the excluded practitioner to take the actions required by § 11.58(b) (e.g., client notification/transfer). Practice outside that narrow purpose/timeframe is not authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of the Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director 'shall publish this Final Order' and 'shall publish the following notice in the Official Gazette' containing the respondent's name, city, licensing status, that the respondent is not a registered patent practitioner, the disciplinary basis (violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)), and a summary of the state-court disbarment and crimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order supplies model notice text showing required elements: respondent identity and locale, licensure status, nature of order (reciprocal discipline/exclusion), citation of the USPTO rules violated, description of the underlying state-court disbarment and criminal convictions (including that the crimes are 'serious crimes'), and statutory/rule authority for the action (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59). Disciplinary decisions are also to be posted for public reading in the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, 'shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires affirmative transmission of the Final Order and reasons to relevant state disciplinary bodies and courts and public notice as prescribed by § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent 'shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order conditions any future reinstatement on full compliance with § 11.60 (the USPTO rule governing reinstatement procedures and standards). Respondent must follow those procedural and substantive requirements when seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond to the Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent 'has not filed a response to the Notice and Order. 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Accordingly, it is hereby determined that: 1) there is no genuine issue of material fact pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and 2) exclusion of Respondent from practice before the USPTO is appropriate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file the required response within the 40-day period supports a determination that no genuine issue of material fact exists and justifies imposition of identical reciprocal discipline without further factual hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of statutory authority and rule citations to justify action
rubrics_metrics.description: The order states the action is 'taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and 11.59.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline and publication/notification practices must be grounded in these statutory and regulatory authorities; any disciplinary action should cite applicable statutes and CFR provisions as support.
